newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: New Schiphol night rules worry air cargo industry.
newsitem.headline: New Schiphol night rules worry air cargo industry.

text.p: ATAN, the Air Transport Association in the Netherlands, is concerned about further night flight restrictions for "the most noisy wide-body aircraft" proposed by Amsterdam Schiphol Airport.
There are fears that this could even effect the work-horse of the industry, the Boeing 747-200, said ATAN spokesman Hans Knuvers.
"We are not happy with this proposal and we believe that the Dutch air cargo community's competitive position will be weakened."
"This is contrary to the Dutch manifesto of being a top player in the global cargo industry."
Schiphol is proposing to introduce the tougher measures on August 1 on take-off flights in the hours from 2300 hours to 0600 hours.
The airport's proposal is awaiting the approval of the government and a decision is expected next week.
In a statement Schiphol said night flight allowances are nearly full because there were more flights in the year than planned and airlines had not been keeping to their schedules.
But Knuvers said "We are still waiting for a decision and these measures are being introduced on August 1. As an industry we did not expect measures like this so soon."
ATAN hopes individual members will be able to change schedules from night to day-time. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
